replay.index_effect: If the gate allowed it: one row keyed 2026-10-08 is added to dates; latest_date stays 2026-10-12 (the max is unchanged); the other ten rows are carried forward unchanged. If the gate refuses it, as the current code does: the index version does not move.
replay.leaves_other_dates_untouched_basis: Code: HoldingsPublication.publish (holdings/publication.py lines 295-298) copies the prior dates and sets only dates[business_date], where business_date is the candidate's clocks.business_date, the custody partition date (holdings_49f.py line 567). Measured: the 2026-10-08 partitions exist and 2026-10-08 is absent from the index (S165 index read; no index version between 2026-10-08T14:20:48Z and 2026-10-12T14:20:43Z). Caveat: publish() does not assert that the landed date equals as_of; a missing 2026-10-08 partition would land an older date and overwrite its row. Filed as IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W381-S3.
replay.gate_refusal_basis: evaluate_publish_gate (holdings_snapshot.py lines 3076-3085): candidate 2026-10-08 against served frontier 2026-10-12; tcal.trading_days_behind(2026-10-08, 2026-10-12) = 2 (run locally on lib/trading_calendar.py, NYSE fallback calendar). Condition source_frontier_older, count 2. The gate runs before land(), so a refused replay writes only the refusal record.
replay.route_needed: The code offers no route for an older date. Options, none chosen here: (a) a gate change, a gap-fill exemption in evaluate_publish_gate for a date absent from the served index, which moves the gate for every firm and every later fire; (b) an operator path past source_frontier_older for one named firm and date, a flag on run_firm or main, which moves the gate for one run only; both need a signed pair (CTO and COO halves) with a ruling that names both branches; (c) no code change: a ruling alone cannot land the replay, because the gate runs on every upload; (d) leave the gap: each attempt rewrites the refusal record. Other gate conditions were not evaluated: no candidate was built.
replay.rollback: Branch B. The served manifest version of the one key current/manifest.json at the 2026-10-14 read is daFZJt6f7G9.CXj3MJftFYV.DNUOVFQh (IsLatest, last modified 2026-10-13T14:20:49Z; list-object-versions). Rollback is a copy-object of that VersionId back onto the key, which makes a new version carrying the prior bytes; that copy is itself a write and needs its own pair. The 2026-10-08 revision objects stay in the bucket as unreferenced immutable objects. Deleting the replay's version instead is destructive and needs Andrew's word.

notes: Base: worktree HEAD before the first commit, 201e7e9c27 (full hash in base_commit). Code read at that commit: data/assets/scripts/gold/investor_reporting/holdings_snapshot.py (main line 3227, run_firm 3133, evaluate_publish_gate 3031, land 2862, served_publication 2955); holdings_49f.py (load_49f_sources 210, build_49f_meshed 625); infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/holdings/publication.py (begin 143, publish 222); holdings_refresh/refresh_dispatch.py; infra/aws/terraform/investor-reporting/directory/holdings_refresh.tf and schedule.tf.

The replay was not run and no candidate was built. Its facts are read from code at the base commit, plus live reads of the source partition listings, the partition write times and the publication index's version list.
Timeout: 3600 is the dispatcher's explicit executionTimeout, and the 3600 TimeoutSeconds on each list-commands item agrees. The dispatcher's own Lambda timeout, 60 seconds, is not the SSM window.

Fire durations: ssm list-commands returned 2967 commands with no NextToken, so the listing is complete within SSM's retained window. Filtered client side on the Comment prefix 'irpt holdings refresh 49financial', it gives 11 scheduled fires, 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-13. Each has one invocation, read with list-command-invocations --details under a --query that projects status, StatusDetails and plugin timestamps only; no output field was read. duration_seconds is RequestedDateTime to the plugin's ResponseFinishDateTime, as the order specifies; plugin_run_seconds (start to finish) is shown beside it.

The 2026-10-09 fire: command status Failed; invocation and plugin status TimedOut; StatusDetails ExecutionTimedOut; response code 137. The plugin ran 309.9 seconds against a 3600-second window. Two other runs were shorter (258.5 s on 2026-09-30 was the shortest), and the 2026-10-07 run took 342.7 s and succeeded. No fire approached 3600 seconds. The cause of the kill was not read (no output) and is not stated here. See IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W381-S1.
The 2026-09-30 fire waited about 252 seconds between RequestedDateTime and plugin start, which is why its duration_seconds (510.6) is the maximum; its plugin run was 258.5 seconds.
